steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Cream together brown sugar, butter, and white sugar in a large bowl until smooth.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in milk and vanilla.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt; stir into sugar mixture until well blended.
Stir in oats, chocolate chips, walnuts, and coconut until evenly distributed.
Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets. Bake in the preheated oven for 10 to 12 minutes for a chewy cookie or 14 minutes for a firmer cookie.
Cool for 1 minute on the cookie sheets and then remove to wire rack. Cool completely and then store in a tightly sealed container.

raw_recipe.headline: Oatmeal Chocolate Coconut Chewy
raw_recipe.description: Irresistible oatmeal coconut cookies full of chocolate chips, shredded coconut, and chopped nuts. Easy to make for a tasty twist on classic treats.
raw_recipe.name: Oatmeal Chocolate Coconut Chewy

review.reviewBody: This is a thousand dollar recipe, I've been looking for something like this for awhile! However, I did make a few modifications to make it more whole grain and wonderfully delicious. I subbed the 1 3/4 cups of flour with 1 cup whole wheat flour and 3/4 cup oat flour, then cut the 1/2 cup of white sugar to 1/4 cup of white sugar (someone on here thought it was too sweet). I also used only 2.5 cups of rolled oats, as that was all that I had left. Another tip - put your cookie dough in the fridge for 1 hour before you start to bake it and use a small icecream scooper to form the cookies on your cookie sheet. It tasted wonderfully chewy, rich and perfectly sweet. It reminded me of the Double Tree Chocolate Chip cookies they used to give out at their hotel, but better because I used all organic ingredients and absolutely no preservatives. Yummy!

This recipe gave me a perfect foundation to tweak to my preference! This says something because it doesn't always work the way I envision it. I substituted 1/2 C of the butter with applesauce; I used whole wheat flour; I used only one C brown sugar and no white sugar (plenty sweet, applesauce helped); I read that someone added a teaspoon of lemon juice to keep the cookies moist, so I tweaked that a bit and added a TBL of lemon juice to the milk (shortcut to buttermilk) and measured my two TBL of milk from there. No nuts in my baked goods. ;-) Also, I have a tendency to over-mix leaving dry cake-like cookies, I was very careful not to do this. They turned out moist and really delicious!

Instead of the coconut, chocolate chips & nuts, I used a 12oz bag of white chips, 1 1/2 c. dried cranberries and 3/4 c.walnuts. Made them much smaller than some have suggested-used a level Tbsp. (#50 scoop). Baked 375 for 10-12 min, depended on cookie sheets used (dark vs. lt. or airbake) if they were more chewy or crunchy. I may have to make another batch to make it through Christmas. (yum)

These turned out great. A bit of trouble with the timing though. After 10 minutes, they seemed raw. After 14, still very doughy. I took them out at 16, though they were still very soft. As they cool, they harden up quite a bit, and 16 minutes was too long. 12 minutes was perfect for the next batch, but just know they’ll come out of the oven still looking underdone.

After reading some people’s came out flat, I refrigerated the dough for an hour first and used parchment paper on the baking sheets. They still flattened some, but they weren’t too thin.

This is the best and only recipe I will ever use again for chocolate chip cookies I used pecans and chunk chocolate chips and white chocolate chips and the new Country Crock plant butter and did like 2 tablespoons of dough to make big cookies and made sure they were pushed all together- outrageous-the best

I thought these were excellent -- loved the texture. I had a butter-flavored Crisco bar I needed to use so I used instead of butter and added 2 extra TBSP milk. Actually, used half and half because that's what I had. Only had a cup of semi-sweet chips. Baked in convection mode so reduced heat 25 degrees and baked 8 minutes on bottom shelf and 2 on top and they browned up and were perfectly chewy. I used a small ice cream scoop and ended up with 48 gorgeous cookies. Per Woody's update I will add a little more coconut next time and hopefully will have a whole bag of chips!

Good base recipe to customize on your own! I browned the butter and let that cool before creaming it with the sugar. I added 1 1/2cups of brown sugar and only 1/4 cup white sugar to make sure that they were chewy. I added only chocolate chips and the oatmeal and they were delicious!

Great cookie. I used 1 c. chocolate and 1 c. butterscotch chips and added 1 c. craisins. Not a fan of walnuts so I used pecans. Baked a little longer so they were crispy/chewy cookies. This recipe is a definite keeper!

Excellent recipe! I only had a stick of butter, and LOVE to bake with coconut oil, so I used a half cup of each. Happy to see the suggestion for using 1 tsp. lemon juice to keep the cookies soft - that def helped. Instead of including nuts, I used 1.5 cups of coconut but only had flakes, so I zapped them in the mini processor for a min. Also only had mini choc chips on hand which were good, but perhaps made the cookies more consistently chocolatey instead of just dots of chocolate. Next time I make these I might try without any chocolate at all and just let the oats and coconut shine.

Just like magic bars, but in a cookie! I packed away most of the dough in snack-sized baggies and froze it, leaving enough for 11 cookies. I think I could get away with less sugar next time...and there will be a next time, but I was amazed that I only ate three and was content. Usually, I don't find cookies at all filling and can down a whole dozen in one sitting. This is why I don't make or buy them. I think the last time I baked a cookie was about twenty years ago! These have some good ingredients: oats, eggs, coconut and walnuts (along with stuff that's not so healthy: butter, sugar and white flour). I love that I can make it once and have eight separate batches when I find myself craving them. I only had frozen butter, so I sliced it up and let it sit for quite a while. When I decided to proceed, the butter still wasn't entirely thawed and was flying out of the bowl when I was trying to use my hand mixer. I did the best I could and then just mixed in the eggs, one at a time. I found it helpful to have bowls of ingredients measured and ready: milk and vanilla in a custard cup, flour, salt and baking soda in a bowl, and the oats, chips, etc in another bowl. When I got to the oats, etc. I mixed the dough with my hand, because it was very dense. Up until that step, I did use the electric hand mixer. Thank you so much for sharing your recipe. It's delicious.

I found these to be very flat and lacked flavor with slightly too dark of edges. Yes, I did use parchment paper as I always do.
After my first batch, I turned down the heat to 350 and added a little more flour, baking powder and chopped butterscotch chips. These came out PERFECT!! The butterscotch picked up the flavor and complimented the rest of the ingredients. Now I would give these 5 stars!

Ive been using this recipe. I repalced the butter for banana. Put a little less sugar. I doubled the milk, cut out nuts and half a cup of chocolate chips to make it low fat. The whole point is to make it low calorie, and it is so good. Thankyou for making such a good recipe.
I followed the recipe as written. Putting the batter in the fridge for 1 hour before baking kept the cookie thick and chewy.

This is my very favorite cookie recipe ever. I don't add nuts. I substitute 1 T. of coconut extract for the vanilla. I cut back on the sugar (1/4 of a cup of white sugar and 1 cup of brown sugar). I add 1 T of baking powder. Sometimes I substitute a half cup of coconut oil for one of the sticks of butter. These are Amazing !!
I loved it so much I’m gifting them out to family for Christmas in bakery boxes & cellophane pockets!
I made these for a family member that loves coconut. I was pleasantly surprised everyone loves them! Great, easy, quick and delicious!

First time I made using coconut flakes. Loved the texture and chewiness. This time I used sweetened shredded and cookies are very sweet. I used 1/2 walnuts and half pepitas. Great recipe. Maybe next time I will use coconut flakes and 1/4 dried apricots.
These cookies are delicious. I have a question. @Woody Broadhurst - Where can I buy the white plastic bowl with spout that is used in the video of this recipe to mix the dry ingredients?
I've been using this recipe for years. It's my fail-poof dessert for any occasion. I've had so many people ask me to share it after trying them. It's perfect as written! Don't change a thing,
Great. Delicious
